selection.explanation: All three candidates pass the 4 tests and implement ISO 8601 duration parsing correctly. The key difference is that candidates n4 and n1 are identical implementations—both contain 221 lines of code with the same parsing logic using regex, identical validation, and identical duration-application algorithms. Candidate n3 uses a more modular approach with separate helper functions (200 lines of core code vs. 221 inline), which is a minor code quality advantage, but it adds a collateral file `quick_test.py` with 27 additional test cases that was not part of the requested task. While this test file demonstrates good practice, the instructions prioritize focused, non-collateral changes. All three correctly handle sign parsing, component validation (order, repetition, fractions only on last component, no fractions on Y/M), weeks-cannot-combine rules, day-of-month overflow, and proper application of months/days/time in sequence. Since n4 and n1 are identical, they both represent the same solution; they rank above n3 due to avoiding the unnecessary test file addition.
